questions.prompt: Which INFO metrics let you compute the cache hit rate?

options.text: used_memory and maxmemory
keyspace_hits and keyspace_misses
connected_clients and blocked_clients
evicted_keys and expired_keys

questions.explanation: The hit rate is keyspace_hits / (keyspace_hits + keyspace_misses). A falling hit rate often signals short TTLs, memory pressure, or eviction churn.

questions.prompt: Why should MONITOR be used only briefly?

options.text: It deletes keys as it runs
It streams every command the server processes, adding significant overhead that can slow a busy server
It disables persistence
It only works once per day

questions.explanation: MONITOR copies every processed command to your connection — great for short debugging but costly at high throughput, so never leave it running in production.

questions.prompt: Which statements about operating Redis are true? Select all that apply.

options.text: Rising evicted_keys indicates memory pressure
Keyspace notifications ride on Pub/Sub, so a disconnected listener can miss events
A rolling upgrade upgrades a replica first, then fails over
MONITOR is the recommended way to continuously watch a production server

questions.explanation: Evictions signal pressure, keyspace notifications are fire-and-forget, and rolling upgrades go replica-first. MONITOR is NOT for continuous monitoring — use INFO/SLOWLOG.

questions.prompt: How do you take a consistent point-in-time backup of Redis data?

options.text: Run MONITOR and save the output
Run BGSAVE to produce a fresh RDB snapshot and copy dump.rdb off-host
Run FLUSHALL first
Delete the AOF file

questions.explanation: BGSAVE creates a consistent RDB snapshot; copy that file off the Redis host so a host failure doesn't take the backups with it.

questions.prompt: The single command that returns grouped server metrics (memory, stats, clients, replication) is ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: INFO returns sections of metrics; INFO <section> (e.g. INFO memory) returns just one.

questions.prompt: What do keyspace notifications allow an application to do?

options.text: Guarantee exactly-once delivery of all key events
Receive Pub/Sub events when keys change or expire, and react to them
Encrypt keys at rest
Automatically back up the keyspace

questions.explanation: With notify-keyspace-events enabled, Redis publishes events (like expired or del) that apps can subscribe to — though, being Pub/Sub, a disconnected listener may miss some.
